title: Stop Trying: Effortless Action and Belief
one_liner: Perceived difficulty is mimetic — stop trying hard and let belief replace effortful thinking.
key_points: Mimicry shapes difficulty: a panda grimaces breaking bamboo because it copied humans, proving nocebo and predictive processing inflate struggle
Girard's mimetic theory says we imitate desires and actions from prestigious mediators, making neutral tasks feel harder than they are
Wu-wei, Stoicism, and Schopenhauer align: the intellect interferes with instinct — strip concepts and personality to act effortlessly
Belief is not gaining new information but forgetting limiting concepts; childlike faith bypasses scheming and dissolves perceived obstacles
